metrics.name: words_missing
metrics.threshold: transcript word(s) with recogniser posterior < 0.1 (reference >= 0.5) squeezed below 55 % of the reference duration

regions.explanation: From 6.40s to 7.52s (“I speak tonight for the”), 3 word(s) of the text were not said (missing: “speak tonight for”; recognised here: “ey spar the”): the recogniser's confidence in them fell to 0.00 against 0.95 in the reference. Leaving out words changes the text the audience hears; in a prepared reading it is scored as an accuracy error, and a missing function word can change the meaning of the sentence. Fix: Slow down slightly through this line and keep your eyes a phrase ahead of your voice.

regions.text: was at Lexington and Concord. So
regions.explanation: From 52.12s to 54.74s (“was at Lexington and Concord. So”), articulation rate was 4.89 syll/s against 3.26 syll/s in the reference (+50%); that is 1.7× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Faster articulation compresses the stressed syllables and the micro-pauses listeners use to segment phrases, so key words lose emphasis and comprehension drops. Fix: Slow to the reference pace here and let the pauses between clauses breathe.
